newsitem.title: MADAGASCAR: Ratsiraka in strong position in Madagascar vote.
newsitem.headline: Ratsiraka in strong position in Madagascar vote.

text.p: Former Madagascan military ruler Didier Ratsiraka looked well placed to win the second round of presidential elections when one of the first-round candidates pledged him his party's support on Thursday.

Millionaire businessman Herizo Razafimahaleo, who took 15.13 percent of the vote in the first round, told a news conference that he and his Leader Fanilo party would now support Ratsiraka against another former president, Albert Zafy.
In the first round on November 3, Ratsiraka won 36.61 percent against 23.39 for Zafy. As the top two candidates, they are the only names on the ballot paper in the second round.
Politicians had expected Razafimahaleo's decision because of his role as economic adviser to Ratsiraka as head of state.
Later on Thursday the government fixed December 29 as the date for the second round. This will become official when Prime Minister Norbert Ratsirahonana, now abroad, signs a decree.

Posts and Telecommunications Minister Ny Hasina Andriamanjato, the son of another first-round candidate, was present at the same news conference alongside Razafimahaleo -- an indication that Ratsiraka may win support there too.

His father, speaker of parliament Richard Andriamanjato, who won 4.94 percent of the first-round vote, says he is not advising his followers how to vote but political analysts say at least some of them will back Ratsiraka.
The election was called after Zafy, 69, who was elected president in place of Ratsiraka in 1993, was impeached by parliament in July for abuse of his authority.

The strength of support for Ratsiraka, a 60-year-old retired admiral, has surprised many observers. He was reviled by many of his people in the early 1990s for using the army to resist the pro-democracy movement on the vast island with a population of 14 million, most of whom live in chronic poverty.
Campaigning for the second round will start on Sunday.
